chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Ivie Anderson
summary: Maxwell adored Ivie Anderson, who knew him as Tracy.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Oh, let's see if I can get something else wrong. Ivey Anderson is married to Bacon, the trumpet player.
I know him. Now, I can't say that. It could be so.
I know, I once proposed to her.
I would have done it too, man.
I once proposed to her and somebody said, oh, she's married to another trumpet player.
Yeah, Louis Bacon. And probably so, it was a little ahead of my time. I didn't know -- Ivy Anderson

lived right in Chicago, she lived one block from me. My mother lives right near there now. But she was already a star and I didn't really know her. She was responsible for getting Jimmy Blanton in the band.

Really? That time I went down to Frisco she'd just started with the band. And I met her there and she always remembered I was from Tracy. And I saw her three years later and she said, Oh, hello, Tracy. And I used to follow her around like a hopeless sheepdog. I was crazy about her.
She's my favorite singer. She's so subtle, blends. Like she made "My Old Flame," "Troubled Waters," some of those beautiful songs, "Lonely Coette" She sang beautiful.
You have such a beautiful knowledge of these things, Jimmy.

Oh, I could sing those for you, start to finish. She was such a sensitive singer. And she's not really very appreciated you know, she gets lost in the shuffle. I guess she didn't have a tragic enough life.
She opened up a restaurant down there.
